So there's a protocol called ActivityPub. It's used for decentralized style social networks. It's like e-mail. You can have a personal e-mail address @yahoo.com that's run by Yahoo, and you might have your company e-mail, bob@somedumpcompany.whatever, and you can e-mail between one and the other because of a decades old ancient standard called SMTP (which forms the backbone of e-mail on the Internet).

There are many e-mail servers (postfix, sendmail, opensmtpd, Exchange, whatever Google wrote in-house) and they can all talk to each other using SMTP (just like Firefox and Chrome can both get websites using HTTP).

ActivityPub addresses look like @someone@example.com. Similar to Twitter handles, but with a domain. You can create an ActivityPub server on a domain and run it yourself. The big AP softwares are Mastodon, Pleroma, Misskey, Hubzilla and Pixelfed. Setting up a server is pretty difficult if you're not in tech/a sys admin, so fear not, you can just join an existing one! (or multiple ones, like getting both a gmail and a yahoo e-mail address).
